edits.text: 1. Purchase Price. The Buyer shall pay the Seller USD 45,000,000 in cash at Closing for the Shares.
2. Closing. Closing shall occur within 30 days after the date of this Agreement, subject to satisfaction or waiver of the conditions to Closing set forth in this Agreement.

3. Representations. The Seller represents, except as set forth in the disclosure schedules, that the financial statements delivered to the Buyer have been prepared in accordance with the applicable accounting principles consistently applied and fairly present, in all material respects, the financial condition and results of operations of the Company as of the dates and for the periods indicated. This representation is made as of the date of this Agreement and, if applicable, as of Closing.

4. Confidentiality. Each party shall keep confidential the terms of this Agreement and the other party’s non-public information received in connection with the transaction, and shall not disclose such information except to its representatives who need to know it and are bound by confidentiality obligations, as required by law or legal process, or with the other party’s prior written consent. This Section does not restrict disclosures of information that is or becomes public other than through a breach of this Agreement.

edits.text: 1. Purchase Price. The Buyer shall pay the Seller USD 45,000,000 in cash at Closing for the Shares, subject only to any purchase-price adjustments expressly set forth in this Agreement. The Buyer’s diligence shall not constitute a condition to payment or give the Buyer a unilateral right to reduce the Purchase Price or terminate this Agreement.

2. Closing. Closing shall occur within 60 days after the date of this Agreement, subject to satisfaction or waiver of the conditions to Closing set forth in this Agreement. If, on that date, a required governmental or regulatory approval remains pending, either party may extend the Closing once for up to 30 days, to the extent reasonably necessary to obtain that approval, provided the party seeking the extension has used reasonable efforts to obtain it.

3. Representations. Except as set forth in the disclosure schedules, the Seller represents to the Buyer as of the date of this Agreement and, if applicable, as of Closing: (a) the financial statements delivered to the Buyer have been prepared in accordance with the accounting principles identified therein, consistently applied, and fairly present in all material respects the financial condition and results of operations of the Company as of the dates and for the periods indicated; (b) the Company is duly organized, validly existing and in good standing, and has the requisite power to own its assets and operate its business as presently conducted; (c) the Company has no liabilities required to be reflected on its financial statements under the applicable accounting principles, other than liabilities reflected or reserved against in those statements, incurred in the ordinary course since the date thereof, or otherwise disclosed in the disclosure schedules; (d) the Company has timely filed material tax returns and paid material taxes due, subject to good-faith contests and adequate reserves; (e) the Company is not in material breach of any material contract to which it is a party, and, to the Seller’s knowledge, no other party is in material breach thereof; (f) the Company is in material compliance with applicable laws and has not received written notice of a material violation that remains unresolved; (g) the Company is in material compliance with applicable employment laws, and there is no pending material employment-related claim of which the Seller has received written notice; and (h) there is no action, suit or proceeding pending, or to the Seller’s knowledge threatened in writing, against the Company that would reasonably be expected to be material to the Company. The foregoing representations are subject to the qualifications expressly stated in this Section and the disclosure schedules.

4. Confidentiality. Each party shall keep confidential the terms of this Agreement and the other party’s non-public information received in connection with the transaction, and shall not disclose such information except to its representatives who need to know it and are bound by confidentiality obligations, to existing or prospective financing sources and their representatives who are bound by confidentiality obligations, as required by law or legal process (with prior notice where legally permitted), or with the other party’s prior written consent. This Section does not restrict information that is or becomes public other than through a breach of this Agreement, is independently developed without use of or reference to the confidential information, or is rightfully received from another source not known to be under a duty of confidentiality with respect to that information.

5. Indemnification. Subject to the limitations in this Section, the Seller shall indemnify the Buyer for direct losses arising from a breach of the Seller’s representations, warranties or covenants in this Agreement and for any liabilities expressly identified as Seller-retained liabilities in the disclosure schedules. Claims for breach of representations and warranties (other than Fundamental Representations) must be asserted within 12 months after Closing; claims for breach of Fundamental Representations must be asserted within six years after Closing; and covenant claims survive for the applicable statute of limitations or the period expressly specified for the covenant. The Seller’s aggregate liability for claims other than Fundamental Representations and fraud shall not exceed 10% of the Purchase Price, and the Seller’s aggregate liability for Fundamental Representations shall not exceed the Purchase Price. The Seller shall have no liability for such claims unless aggregate covered losses exceed 1% of the Purchase Price, in which case liability shall apply only to losses in excess of that amount. A portion equal to 5% of the Purchase Price shall be placed in escrow at Closing for 12 months as the Buyer’s exclusive source of recovery for claims subject to the general cap and basket, with unused amounts released to the Seller at the end of that period. No party may recover more than once for the same loss, and consequential, punitive and exemplary damages and lost profits shall be excluded except to the extent awarded to a third party or arising from fraud. The limitations in this Section do not apply to fraud or a party’s intentional breach of its covenants. “Fundamental Representations” means the Seller’s representations concerning organization, authority, title to the Shares and brokers.

Preserve the Buyer’s price position while proposing a defined, objective purchase-price adjustment mechanism rather than conceding USD 45 million. The expanded representations are useful, but their value depends on receiving and reviewing complete disclosure schedules. The indemnity terms shown in tracked changes are materially Seller-favorable: the 1% basket is a deductible, the 5% escrow is the exclusive recovery source for general claims, and the 10% cap and 12-month survival are restrictive. receiver.requested_changes: Please confirm whether the indemnity text appearing in tracked changes is the Seller’s current proposal, and provide a clean draft identifying all proposed operative terms. We cannot evaluate the representations without the disclosure schedules; please circulate complete schedules promptly and allow the Buyer a reasonable review period before signing. Please add an objective, expressly defined closing adjustment for cash, indebtedness, transaction expenses and working capital against an agreed target, with a post-closing statement, a defined dispute process and access to supporting records. This is a bounded calculation, not an open-ended diligence or unilateral termination right. We continue to propose USD 40,000,000, subject to that defined adjustment and satisfactory review of the schedules; alternatively, please provide the Seller’s counterproposal. For indemnification, propose a 24-month survival period for general representations, a 6-year period for fundamental and tax representations, and survival for covenants as specified or under the applicable limitation period. The general basket should be a tipping basket, not a deductible; the general cap should be at least 20% of the Purchase Price, with no cap for fundamental, tax, or fraud claims. Fundamental representations should include organization, authority, title, capitalization and brokers. The escrow should not be the exclusive source of recovery, and its amount and duration should provide meaningful security for claims. Please also clarify that the damages exclusion does not bar reasonably foreseeable losses, diminution in value, or losses recoverable under the indemnity, while retaining the no-double-recovery protection. The 60-day closing period and one regulatory extension are acceptable in principle, subject to reasonable efforts and appropriate closing conditions. Confidentiality exceptions for financing sources are acceptable if disclosures are limited to information reasonably necessary for financing and those sources are bound by confidentiality obligations at least as protective as this provision.
receiver.message_back: Thank you for the revised draft. The expanded representations, regulatory closing extension and financing-source confidentiality exception are constructive. We cannot accept USD 45 million without a defined adjustment mechanism and review of the disclosure schedules. Our proposal remains USD 40 million, with a narrowly defined adjustment for cash, indebtedness, transaction expenses and working capital, calculated under an agreed process. Please circulate the schedules and confirm whether the indemnity language shown in tracked changes reflects the Seller’s current proposal; it is not yet clear to us that this language is intended as operative text. We have set out proposed revisions to the indemnity framework above. The price and indemnity positions remain subject to agreement on the full documentation.
